help_doc     crates/chat-stasher/src/main.rs:420  The first line answers the question the timer cannot: it reads the
help_doc     crates/chat-stasher/src/main.rs:421  `run-state.json` written by the last `run-once` pass. Three distinct
help_doc     crates/chat-stasher/src/main.rs:422  answers, and only the first is a healthy one:
help_doc     crates/chat-stasher/src/main.rs:423
help_doc     crates/chat-stasher/src/main.rs:424  * last run recent and successful -> exit 0
help_doc     crates/chat-stasher/src/main.rs:425  * last run FAILED -> exit 1, saying which step failed
help_doc     crates/chat-stasher/src/main.rs:426  * no run recorded at all, or nothing has run for longer than
help_doc     crates/chat-stasher/src/main.rs:427    4x `backup_interval_secs` (minimum 1 hour) -> exit 1. A dead timer
help_doc     crates/chat-stasher/src/main.rs:428    usually leaves a *successful* last run behind, so this overdue check
help_doc     crates/chat-stasher/src/main.rs:429    is the only thing that catches it.
help_doc     crates/chat-stasher/src/main.rs:430
help_doc     crates/chat-stasher/src/main.rs:431  Never prints session content: counts, timestamps and digests only.
help_doc     crates/chat-stasher/src/main.rs:432
help_doc     crates/chat-stasher/src/main.rs:433  Default output is a handful of lines and nothing more: the verdict
help_doc     crates/chat-stasher/src/main.rs:434  above, then aggregate scan counts (per-harness session totals, skipped
help_doc     crates/chat-stasher/src/main.rs:435  roots, unarchivable-session warning). It stays that size whether the
help_doc     crates/chat-stasher/src/main.rs:436  machine holds three sessions or three thousand, so the verdict never
help_doc     crates/chat-stasher/src/main.rs:437  scrolls away.
help_doc     crates/chat-stasher/src/main.rs:438

help_doc     crates/chat-stasher/src/main.rs:441  id). That is the troubleshooting view; it can be hundreds of lines.
help_doc     crates/chat-stasher/src/main.rs:443  Also print one metadata line per session found (can be hundreds).
help_doc     crates/chat-stasher/src/main.rs:446  Print exactly one JSON object to stdout and nothing else (the
help_doc     crates/chat-stasher/src/main.rs:447  human lines still go to stderr). Tri-state fields are tagged
help_doc     crates/chat-stasher/src/main.rs:448  `{"kind":"known",…}` / `{"kind":"unknown","why":…}` /
help_doc     crates/chat-stasher/src/main.rs:449  `{"kind":"not_applicable",…}` — an unknown is never serialised as
help_doc     crates/chat-stasher/src/main.rs:450  `0`, `null` or a missing field. `run_state.kind` is
help_doc     crates/chat-stasher/src/main.rs:451  `known` / `missing` / `unreadable`; `scanner.kind` is `ok` /
help_doc     crates/chat-stasher/src/main.rs:452  `failed`. `exit_semantics` documents what the exit code means.

help_doc     crates/chat-stasher/src/main.rs:474  Read one session from the repository (sequence-concatenated) and
help_doc     crates/chat-stasher/src/main.rs:475  report its length and sha256 without printing content. With `--all-machines`, walk
help_doc     crates/chat-stasher/src/main.rs:476  **every snapshot of every machine** cumulatively and report per-session
help_doc     crates/chat-stasher/src/main.rs:477  digests.
help_doc     crates/chat-stasher/src/main.rs:479  Local stage directory to compare the read against. Optional: the

help_doc     crates/chat-stasher/src/main.rs:481  `--machine` and `--session`, and this only adds an

help_doc     crates/chat-stasher/src/main.rs:483  disk. It does **not** have to be the archiving machine's stage root,
help_doc     crates/chat-stasher/src/main.rs:484  and a path that does not exist merely leaves that line uncomputed.

help_doc     crates/chat-stasher/src/main.rs:489  every snapshot of `--machine`, newest first, so a session reclaimed
help_doc     crates/chat-stasher/src/main.rs:490  out of the stage is still readable. Ignored by `--all-machines`.
help_doc     crates/chat-stasher/src/main.rs:493  Cross-machine merge, cumulative: for every hostname, every snapshot
help_doc     crates/chat-stasher/src/main.rs:494  (`sessions/<machine>/…`), each session's shards sequence-joined and
help_doc     crates/chat-stasher/src/main.rs:495  hashed. Newest copies per shard path win; older sequences absent from
help_doc     crates/chat-stasher/src/main.rs:496  newer snapshots remain included. Prints ids, counts, lengths, and sha256 only.
help_doc     crates/chat-stasher/src/main.rs:499  Print full session ids in per-session rows (default: privacy-safe short ids).
help_doc     crates/chat-stasher/src/main.rs:502  Show every stored shard. Default reads collapse legacy whole-content
help_doc     crates/chat-stasher/src/main.rs:503  replays while retaining verified sequence-bound captures, including
help_doc     crates/chat-stasher/src/main.rs:504  identical captured bodies. Nothing is deleted by either policy.
help_doc     crates/chat-stasher/src/main.rs:507  Machine partition to read. Uses this machine's id when available;
help_doc     crates/chat-stasher/src/main.rs:508  if it is unavailable, use `--machine` explicitly. Unused by
help_doc     crates/chat-stasher/src/main.rs:509  `--all-machines`, which reads every machine.

help_doc     crates/chat-stasher/src/main.rs:604  Keep ssh ControlMaster processes open after this run.
help_doc     crates/chat-stasher/src/main.rs:608  Initialise a new destination as a *full extra copy* (ADR-013).
help_doc     crates/chat-stasher/src/main.rs:609
help_doc     crates/chat-stasher/src/main.rs:610  Order is fixed: re-collect from the local sources first (they are the
help_doc     crates/chat-stasher/src/main.rs:611  truth, and rereading them puts no load on an existing destination),
help_doc     crates/chat-stasher/src/main.rs:612  then copy back only what an existing destination holds and the local
help_doc     crates/chat-stasher/src/main.rs:613  source no longer does, then push the result. The new destination ends
help_doc     crates/chat-stasher/src/main.rs:614  up with `local ∪ existing destinations`.
help_doc     crates/chat-stasher/src/main.rs:615
help_doc     crates/chat-stasher/src/main.rs:616  A source destination that cannot be consulted makes the difference set
help_doc     crates/chat-stasher/src/main.rs:617  *incomplete*: that is reported and the command exits non-zero. It is
help_doc     crates/chat-stasher/src/main.rs:618  never treated as "that destination had nothing extra".

help_doc     crates/chat-stasher/src/main.rs:649  Keep the ssh ControlMaster processes open after this run (do not shut them down).
help_doc     crates/chat-stasher/src/main.rs:652  Record this destination's ssh host key in `~/.ssh/known_hosts` after
help_doc     crates/chat-stasher/src/main.rs:653  printing its fingerprint. Off by default and never implied: without
help_doc     crates/chat-stasher/src/main.rs:654  this flag nothing is ever written to `known_hosts`, so the first
help_doc     crates/chat-stasher/src/main.rs:655  connection of an unattended run cannot silently trust a host.
help_doc     crates/chat-stasher/src/main.rs:659  Search one destination's archive by session metadata.
help_doc     crates/chat-stasher/src/main.rs:660
help_doc     crates/chat-stasher/src/main.rs:661  Metadata tier only: this walks snapshot/index/tree objects plus each
help_doc     crates/chat-stasher/src/main.rs:662  machine's small activity index, and never fetches or decrypts a
help_doc     crates/chat-stasher/src/main.rs:663  session's conversation shard, which is why it is cheap. On a local
help_doc     crates/chat-stasher/src/main.rs:664  three-session fixture the metadata walk read 11,761 bytes against
help_doc     crates/chat-stasher/src/main.rs:665  1,206,285 bytes of data packs — two orders of magnitude apart.
help_doc     crates/chat-stasher/src/main.rs:666  In a separate metadata-only run, use `--cost` to estimate the payload
help_doc     crates/chat-stasher/src/main.rs:667  size before choosing a full-text mode. `--scan` reads those payloads;
help_doc     crates/chat-stasher/src/main.rs:668  `--text` uses the local index and checks that it covers the selected
help_doc     crates/chat-stasher/src/main.rs:669  sessions before treating zero hits as a complete answer.
help_doc     crates/chat-stasher/src/main.rs:670
help_doc     crates/chat-stasher/src/main.rs:671  One destination per run, always named: there is no automatic merge
help_doc     crates/chat-stasher/src/main.rs:672  across destinations, and no default destination to search "everything".
help_doc     crates/chat-stasher/src/main.rs:673
help_doc     crates/chat-stasher/src/main.rs:674  The time window filters on the **conversation's own activity interval**,
help_doc     crates/chat-stasher/src/main.rs:675  not on when the backup ran: a session matches when `[first message,
help_doc     crates/chat-stasher/src/main.rs:676  last message]` intersects the window. Those times come from the
help_doc     crates/chat-stasher/src/main.rs:677  `activity-index` sidecar (`meta/<machine>/activity-v1.jsonl`) carried in
help_doc     crates/chat-stasher/src/main.rs:678  the archive, so `--day 2026-01-15` finds a conversation held that day
help_doc     crates/chat-stasher/src/main.rs:679  even if the machine was last pushed months later.
help_doc     crates/chat-stasher/src/main.rs:680
help_doc     crates/chat-stasher/src/main.rs:681  A session whose conversation time is unknown is **never silently
help_doc     crates/chat-stasher/src/main.rs:682  excluded**. It is listed separately with the reason, and while a time
help_doc     crates/chat-stasher/src/main.rs:683  window is active it does not count as a match — which also means a
help_doc     crates/chat-stasher/src/main.rs:684  "0 matched" answer cannot be trusted while any remain, so the exit code
help_doc     crates/chat-stasher/src/main.rs:685  is `3` rather than `1`.
help_doc     crates/chat-stasher/src/main.rs:686
help_doc     crates/chat-stasher/src/main.rs:687  `--text` searches the local FTS5 trigram index (substring matching for
help_doc     crates/chat-stasher/src/main.rs:688  runs of at least three characters). A shorter query is refused, not
help_doc     crates/chat-stasher/src/main.rs:689  answered: the report says `matched=unknown` and the run exits `3`.
help_doc     crates/chat-stasher/src/main.rs:690  `--scan` reads selected conversations and matches them as plain text
help_doc     crates/chat-stasher/src/main.rs:691  instead; it answers short queries, at the cost of reading them.
help_doc     crates/chat-stasher/src/main.rs:692
help_doc     crates/chat-stasher/src/main.rs:693  Exit codes distinguish the three answers, because two of them look the
help_doc     crates/chat-stasher/src/main.rs:694  same and mean opposite things: `0` matched something, `1` read the whole
help_doc     crates/chat-stasher/src/main.rs:695  destination and answered for every session with no match, `3` could not
help_doc     crates/chat-stasher/src/main.rs:696  finish — reading it, placing every session in time, or evaluating the
help_doc     crates/chat-stasher/src/main.rs:697  query — so a zero proves nothing. `2` is a usage error, as elsewhere.
help_doc     crates/chat-stasher/src/main.rs:699  Destination to search. Required unless an explicit `--repo` is given.
help_doc     crates/chat-stasher/src/main.rs:702  The shared filters (session / machine / harness / time window).
help_doc     crates/chat-stasher/src/main.rs:705  Search indexed titles and user/assistant text with SQLite's trigram tokenizer.
help_doc     crates/chat-stasher/src/main.rs:708  Read selected sessions and perform a case-insensitive substring scan.
help_doc     crates/chat-stasher/src/main.rs:711  Emit one JSON object on stdout. Metadata searches include separate
help_doc     crates/chat-stasher/src/main.rs:712  matched / not matched / could-not-be-placed groups; text searches
help_doc     crates/chat-stasher/src/main.rs:713  carry coverage, read failures and a `query_state` for the query.
help_doc     crates/chat-stasher/src/main.rs:716  Also report what a full-text pass over the hits would cost.
help_doc     crates/chat-stasher/src/main.rs:719  Repository path override.

help_doc     crates/chat-stasher/src/main.rs:731  Keep the ssh ControlMaster processes open after this run (do not shut them down).
help_doc     crates/chat-stasher/src/main.rs:735  Write every session the shared selector selects to files.
help_doc     crates/chat-stasher/src/main.rs:736
help_doc     crates/chat-stasher/src/main.rs:737  One destination per run, always named, exactly like `search` — and the
help_doc     crates/chat-stasher/src/main.rs:738  selection is literally the same code path: `export` writes the sessions
help_doc     crates/chat-stasher/src/main.rs:739  `search` returns for the same flags, so `search` is the dry run of this
help_doc     crates/chat-stasher/src/main.rs:740  command with a different name, and `--dry-run` prints the same price
help_doc     crates/chat-stasher/src/main.rs:741  `search --cost` reports before anything is fetched.
help_doc     crates/chat-stasher/src/main.rs:742
help_doc     crates/chat-stasher/src/main.rs:743  Layout: `<out>/<machine>/<harness>/<session-id>.jsonl`, each file holding
help_doc     crates/chat-stasher/src/main.rs:744  that session's archived lines in their native format, byte-identical to
help_doc     crates/chat-stasher/src/main.rs:745  what `read` returns for it. Plus `<out>/manifest.json`: per session its
help_doc     crates/chat-stasher/src/main.rs:746  machine, harness, id, first and last message time, shard count, bytes
help_doc     crates/chat-stasher/src/main.rs:747  written, sha256 of the written file and the filters that were applied —
help_doc     crates/chat-stasher/src/main.rs:748  and, at the top level, the sessions no filter could place, the machines
help_doc     crates/chat-stasher/src/main.rs:749  whose activity index could not be read, the sessions that could not be
help_doc     crates/chat-stasher/src/main.rs:750  written, and the exit status this run returns.
help_doc     crates/chat-stasher/src/main.rs:751
help_doc     crates/chat-stasher/src/main.rs:752  `--turns user` keeps only the lines that are the user's own messages.
help_doc     crates/chat-stasher/src/main.rs:753  That is answerable only where the harness's format makes it certain (see
help_doc     crates/chat-stasher/src/main.rs:754  `export::USER_TURNS_HARNESSES`); elsewhere every line is written and the
help_doc     crates/chat-stasher/src/main.rs:755  session records `turns_filter: "not-supported"`. The flag is never
help_doc     crates/chat-stasher/src/main.rs:756  silently ignored and content is never silently dropped.
help_doc     crates/chat-stasher/src/main.rs:757
help_doc     crates/chat-stasher/src/main.rs:758  `--trim-to-window` drops lines whose own timestamp is outside
help_doc     crates/chat-stasher/src/main.rs:759  `--day`/`--since`/`--until`. A line whose timestamp cannot be read is
help_doc     crates/chat-stasher/src/main.rs:760  kept and counted in `untimed_lines`.
help_doc     crates/chat-stasher/src/main.rs:761
help_doc     crates/chat-stasher/src/main.rs:762  `--out` must be empty or absent unless `--force` is given. Nothing is
help_doc     crates/chat-stasher/src/main.rs:763  ever deleted, and nothing is ever written outside `--out`.
help_doc     crates/chat-stasher/src/main.rs:764
help_doc     crates/chat-stasher/src/main.rs:765  Exit codes, the same family `search` uses: `0` wrote at least one
help_doc     crates/chat-stasher/src/main.rs:766  session and answered every session the query touched · `1` read the
help_doc     crates/chat-stasher/src/main.rs:767  whole destination and selected nothing · `3` did not finish — part of
help_doc     crates/chat-stasher/src/main.rs:768  the archive was unreadable, a session could not be placed, or a selected
help_doc     crates/chat-stasher/src/main.rs:769  session could not be written — so the output on disk is real but
help_doc     crates/chat-stasher/src/main.rs:770  incomplete, and the manifest says what is missing · `2` usage error.
help_doc     crates/chat-stasher/src/main.rs:772  Destination to export from. Required unless an explicit `--repo` is given.
help_doc     crates/chat-stasher/src/main.rs:775  Directory to write into. Must be empty or absent unless `--force`.
help_doc     crates/chat-stasher/src/main.rs:778  The shared filters (session / machine / harness / time window).
help_doc     crates/chat-stasher/src/main.rs:781  Which lines to write: `all` (default), or `user` for only the user's
help_doc     crates/chat-stasher/src/main.rs:782  own messages — kept only for harnesses whose format makes that
help_doc     crates/chat-stasher/src/main.rs:783  certain; for any other harness every line is written and the
help_doc     crates/chat-stasher/src/main.rs:784  manifest records `turns_filter: "not-supported"`.
help_doc     crates/chat-stasher/src/main.rs:787  With a time window, also drop lines whose own timestamp lies outside
help_doc     crates/chat-stasher/src/main.rs:788  it. Lines whose time cannot be read are kept and counted in the
help_doc     crates/chat-stasher/src/main.rs:789  manifest's `untimed_lines`. Requires a window.
help_doc     crates/chat-stasher/src/main.rs:792  Write into a non-empty `--out`. Nothing is ever deleted, so files
help_doc     crates/chat-stasher/src/main.rs:793  from an earlier export stay where they are.
help_doc     crates/chat-stasher/src/main.rs:796  Write every stored shard. By default a run that byte-for-byte
help_doc     crates/chat-stasher/src/main.rs:797  replays the session's complete preceding shard sequence is collapsed
help_doc     crates/chat-stasher/src/main.rs:798  to its first copy, because that is what a re-seal leaves. The archive
help_doc     crates/chat-stasher/src/main.rs:799  is never modified either way.
help_doc     crates/chat-stasher/src/main.rs:802  Print the plan and stop: no directory is created and no file is
help_doc     crates/chat-stasher/src/main.rs:803  written.
help_doc     crates/chat-stasher/src/main.rs:806  Repository path override.
help_doc     crates/chat-stasher/src/main.rs:809  Masterkey file override.
help_doc     crates/chat-stasher/src/main.rs:812  Concurrency cap override.
help_doc     crates/chat-stasher/src/main.rs:815  Backend option `key=value`, repeatable.
help_doc     crates/chat-stasher/src/main.rs:818  Keep the ssh ControlMaster processes open after this run (do not shut them down).
help_doc     crates/chat-stasher/src/main.rs:822  Open the archive dashboard in a browser: totals, the machine × source
help_doc     crates/chat-stasher/src/main.rs:823  matrix, a weekly activity heatmap, and drill-down into any cell.
help_doc     crates/chat-stasher/src/main.rs:824
help_doc     crates/chat-stasher/src/main.rs:825  Binds a short-lived HTTP server on `127.0.0.1` with an OS-assigned port
help_doc     crates/chat-stasher/src/main.rs:826  (never `0.0.0.0`, never a fixed port), prints the URL, optionally opens
help_doc     crates/chat-stasher/src/main.rs:827  your browser, and exits when idle or on Ctrl+C. Nothing is installed:
help_doc     crates/chat-stasher/src/main.rs:828  no launchd, no systemd, no background process, no resident daemon.
help_doc     crates/chat-stasher/src/main.rs:829
help_doc     crates/chat-stasher/src/main.rs:830  THREAT, stated plainly: loopback is NOT a security boundary. Every other
help_doc     crates/chat-stasher/src/main.rs:831  program running on this machine can connect to `127.0.0.1`, so this is
help_doc     crates/chat-stasher/src/main.rs:832  not "safe because it's local". Access is gated by a random token that is
help_doc     crates/chat-stasher/src/main.rs:833  generated fresh on every launch and appears only in the printed URL —
help_doc     crates/chat-stasher/src/main.rs:834  never in a file, never in a log. Requests without that exact token are
help_doc     crates/chat-stasher/src/main.rs:835  refused (403), and any method other than GET is refused (405). Treat the
help_doc     crates/chat-stasher/src/main.rs:836  URL as a secret for the lifetime of the process.
help_doc     crates/chat-stasher/src/main.rs:837
help_doc     crates/chat-stasher/src/main.rs:838  Metadata tier: the dashboard and every list are rendered from one read of
help_doc     crates/chat-stasher/src/main.rs:839  snapshot + index + tree metadata plus the activity sidecar. The only
help_doc     crates/chat-stasher/src/main.rs:840  conversation text that read carries is each session's one-line label
help_doc     crates/chat-stasher/src/main.rs:841  (at most 100 characters, recorded in the activity index); a session's
help_doc     crates/chat-stasher/src/main.rs:842  full conversation is fetched and decrypted only when you click it and
help_doc     crates/chat-stasher/src/main.rs:843  then click "load", and the byte cost is printed before you do. Exit
help_doc     crates/chat-stasher/src/main.rs:844  codes: 0 served the dashboard — even an archive that holds nothing,
help_doc     crates/chat-stasher/src/main.rs:845  which is served as an honest empty page rather than not starting; 3
help_doc     crates/chat-stasher/src/main.rs:846  could not finish reading (or no key), and is also the exit status after
help_doc     crates/chat-stasher/src/main.rs:847  serving an archive that could not be read in full; 2 is a usage error.
help_doc     crates/chat-stasher/src/main.rs:849  Deprecated alias for `ui`; prints a one-line notice on stderr and behaves
help_doc     crates/chat-stasher/src/main.rs:850  identically. Kept for one release.
help_doc     crates/chat-stasher/src/main.rs:852  Backfill the audit sidecar from historical sealed bodies without rewriting them.
help_doc     crates/chat-stasher/src/main.rs:854  Stage receiving the derived sidecar; source bodies remain untouched.
help_doc     crates/chat-stasher/src/main.rs:857  Partition owned by this writer.
help_doc     crates/chat-stasher/src/main.rs:860  Retained archive-wide random secret (exactly 32 bytes), outside stage.
help_doc     crates/chat-stasher/src/main.rs:863  Scan only the stage, explicitly excluding historical destination bodies.
help_doc     crates/chat-stasher/src/main.rs:873  Import one official export: archive the file byte-exact, and write one
help_doc     crates/chat-stasher/src/main.rs:874  inbox bundle per conversation into a local inbox.
help_doc     crates/chat-stasher/src/main.rs:875
help_doc     crates/chat-stasher/src/main.rs:876  Reads `<export>` whole, stores it under
help_doc     crates/chat-stasher/src/main.rs:877  `<stage>/import-raw/<platform>/<sha256>` — a sibling of `sessions/`, so it
help_doc     crates/chat-stasher/src/main.rs:878  is in no session count — and writes one `chat-stasher/inbox@3`
help_doc     crates/chat-stasher/src/main.rs:879  `web-capture` bundle per conversation into `--inbox`. A later
help_doc     crates/chat-stasher/src/main.rs:880  `ingest --inbox` is what seals them; this command never seals, never
help_doc     crates/chat-stasher/src/main.rs:881  pushes, never reads config, a destination or a machine identity, and never
help_doc     crates/chat-stasher/src/main.rs:882  modifies or moves the export file.
help_doc     crates/chat-stasher/src/main.rs:883
help_doc     crates/chat-stasher/src/main.rs:884  Only Claude's `conversations.json` has a parser in this build; naming any
help_doc     crates/chat-stasher/src/main.rs:885  other platform is a refusal, not a guess. The archive comparison that would
help_doc     crates/chat-stasher/src/main.rs:886  suppress a body already archived is behind a probe that this build ships
help_doc     crates/chat-stasher/src/main.rs:887  unwired, so every conversation currently gets a body.

help_doc     crates/chat-stasher/src/main.rs:999  Reclaim the sealed shard body from the staging tree, but only where the
help_doc     crates/chat-stasher/src/main.rs:1000  archive provably holds every byte (ADR-020 Phase 4).
help_doc     crates/chat-stasher/src/main.rs:1001
help_doc     crates/chat-stasher/src/main.rs:1002  The stage is an unbounded local full copy; nothing ever shrinks it.
help_doc     crates/chat-stasher/src/main.rs:1003  This command retires the shard body once every declared destination
help_doc     crates/chat-stasher/src/main.rs:1004  proves it holds each session. Proof means asking the archive itself —
help_doc     crates/chat-stasher/src/main.rs:1005  never the local cursor — for every session's digest triple (shard
help_doc     crates/chat-stasher/src/main.rs:1006  count / concatenated bytes / concatenated sha256) and matching it
help_doc     crates/chat-stasher/src/main.rs:1007  against the stage. A destination that cannot be consulted is
help_doc     crates/chat-stasher/src/main.rs:1008  "unproven" and blocks the reclaim: it is never treated as "does not
help_doc     crates/chat-stasher/src/main.rs:1009  have it". Every declared destination must prove it holds each session,
help_doc     crates/chat-stasher/src/main.rs:1010  or
help_doc     crates/chat-stasher/src/main.rs:1011  nothing is deleted.
help_doc     crates/chat-stasher/src/main.rs:1012
help_doc     crates/chat-stasher/src/main.rs:1013  Default is a dry run that reports what would be reclaimed and deletes
help_doc     crates/chat-stasher/src/main.rs:1014  nothing; pass `--apply` to actually remove the body. `--apply` writes
help_doc     crates/chat-stasher/src/main.rs:1015  each machine's retained summaries first, then deletes session by
help_doc     crates/chat-stasher/src/main.rs:1016  session, keeping each session's persistent `shard-seq` counter so the
help_doc     crates/chat-stasher/src/main.rs:1017  next sequence never falls back onto archived shard names.

help_doc     crates/chat-stasher/src/main.rs:1045  Report the packs one destination's backend holds that **no index file
help_doc     crates/chat-stasher/src/main.rs:1046  names** — what a push killed between its packs and its index strands —
help_doc     crates/chat-stasher/src/main.rs:1047  and say what the next push would do about each. Deletes nothing; there
help_doc     crates/chat-stasher/src/main.rs:1048  is no mode in this build that deletes.
help_doc     crates/chat-stasher/src/main.rs:1049
help_doc     crates/chat-stasher/src/main.rs:1050  Dry run is the only mode. `--apply` is refused with exit `3`, naming
help_doc     crates/chat-stasher/src/main.rs:1051  what a safe delete would need and this build does not have: a
help_doc     crates/chat-stasher/src/main.rs:1052  repository-wide lock every client honors, a conditional delete carrying
help_doc     crates/chat-stasher/src/main.rs:1053  an object version, and a trustworthy backend modification time to age
help_doc     crates/chat-stasher/src/main.rs:1054  candidates by. "Unindexed" means no index file names the pack, not that
help_doc     crates/chat-stasher/src/main.rs:1055  the pack is unused — a retry can reuse one and write a snapshot that
help_doc     crates/chat-stasher/src/main.rs:1056  depends on it while it stays unindexed on disk — so the gap is real, not
help_doc     crates/chat-stasher/src/main.rs:1057  a formality.
help_doc     crates/chat-stasher/src/main.rs:1058
help_doc     crates/chat-stasher/src/main.rs:1059  Every pack it reports is verified the way the adopting open verifies one
help_doc     crates/chat-stasher/src/main.rs:1060  before reusing it: the header must decrypt, every blob it declares must
help_doc     crates/chat-stasher/src/main.rs:1061  decrypt and hash to the id the header gives, and the pack's bytes must
help_doc     crates/chat-stasher/src/main.rs:1062  hash to the id it is stored under. A pack that fails any of those is
help_doc     crates/chat-stasher/src/main.rs:1063  reported **unknown** with the verifier's reason, never as empty and
help_doc     crates/chat-stasher/src/main.rs:1064  never as zero, and its presence makes the whole survey incomplete.
help_doc     crates/chat-stasher/src/main.rs:1065
help_doc     crates/chat-stasher/src/main.rs:1066  Reads only: nothing is written to the repository, to an index file or to
help_doc     crates/chat-stasher/src/main.rs:1067  a pack. The report carries the repository fingerprint, the backend
help_doc     crates/chat-stasher/src/main.rs:1068  family, pack and byte totals, the unindexed packs by id prefix and size,
help_doc     crates/chat-stasher/src/main.rs:1069  what the next push would adopt, and any pack an index names that the
help_doc     crates/chat-stasher/src/main.rs:1070  backend does not list. It never carries a path, a host, a machine or an
help_doc     crates/chat-stasher/src/main.rs:1071  account name, or any conversation text.
help_doc     crates/chat-stasher/src/main.rs:1072
help_doc     crates/chat-stasher/src/main.rs:1073  Exit codes: 0 = the survey finished and read every pack; 1 = the survey
help_doc     crates/chat-stasher/src/main.rs:1074  finished and found a contradiction (an index naming a pack the backend
help_doc     crates/chat-stasher/src/main.rs:1075  does not have); 3 = it did not finish reading — a pack or an index file

help_doc     crates/chat-stasher/src/main.rs:1111  Register this executable as the browsers' Native Messaging host
help_doc     crates/chat-stasher/src/main.rs:1112  (ADR-014 step 2) — or, with `--uninstall`, remove that registration.
help_doc     crates/chat-stasher/src/main.rs:1113
help_doc     crates/chat-stasher/src/main.rs:1114  ADR-014 exists because `chrome.downloads` with `saveAs: false` is
help_doc     crates/chat-stasher/src/main.rs:1115  overridden by the browser-level "ask where to save each file before
help_doc     crates/chat-stasher/src/main.rs:1116  downloading" preference, which no extension flag can suppress. At up to
help_doc     crates/chat-stasher/src/main.rs:1117  200 backfilled conversations a day that is 200 modal dialogs.
help_doc     crates/chat-stasher/src/main.rs:1118
help_doc     crates/chat-stasher/src/main.rs:1119  This is one command instead of the five physical actions Native
help_doc     crates/chat-stasher/src/main.rs:1120  Messaging otherwise costs: it renders the host manifest (`name` /
help_doc     crates/chat-stasher/src/main.rs:1121  `description` / the absolute `path` of *this* executable / `type:
help_doc     crates/chat-stasher/src/main.rs:1122  stdio` / the pinned extension allowlist) and drops it into each
help_doc     crates/chat-stasher/src/main.rs:1123  installed browser's discovery directory. No elevation: everything is
help_doc     crates/chat-stasher/src/main.rs:1124  per-user.
help_doc     crates/chat-stasher/src/main.rs:1125
help_doc     crates/chat-stasher/src/main.rs:1126  Every path written, left alone, skipped or removed is printed
help_doc     crates/chat-stasher/src/main.rs:1127  absolutely. "No error" is not the same claim as "a file landed".
help_doc     crates/chat-stasher/src/main.rs:1128
help_doc     crates/chat-stasher/src/main.rs:1129  Idempotent: run it twice and there is exactly one manifest per browser,
help_doc     crates/chat-stasher/src/main.rs:1130  byte-identical, exit 0 both times. Exit codes: 0 = at least one manifest
help_doc     crates/chat-stasher/src/main.rs:1131  is in place (or, for `--uninstall`, removal finished), 3 = nothing was
help_doc     crates/chat-stasher/src/main.rs:1132  written because no known browser was found, 2 = usage error (bad host
help_doc     crates/chat-stasher/src/main.rs:1133  name / extension id / relative binary path), 1 = an action failed.
help_doc     crates/chat-stasher/src/main.rs:1135  Browser to register with, repeatable. Default: every browser whose
help_doc     crates/chat-stasher/src/main.rs:1136  data directory exists on this machine. Naming one explicitly writes
help_doc     crates/chat-stasher/src/main.rs:1137  it even when that directory is absent.
help_doc     crates/chat-stasher/src/main.rs:1140  Discovery root override (macOS default: `~/Library/Application
help_doc     crates/chat-stasher/src/main.rs:1141  Support`). This is what makes the command testable without writing
help_doc     crates/chat-stasher/src/main.rs:1142  into a real browser directory.
help_doc     crates/chat-stasher/src/main.rs:1145  Which OS path layout to use. Default: this platform.
help_doc     crates/chat-stasher/src/main.rs:1148  Host binary recorded in the manifest. Default: this executable
help_doc     crates/chat-stasher/src/main.rs:1149  (`std::env::current_exe()`), which is the only value that stays
help_doc     crates/chat-stasher/src/main.rs:1150  correct after `cargo install --force`.
help_doc     crates/chat-stasher/src/main.rs:1153  Host name override. Chromium's grammar is `[a-z0-9_.]` only.
help_doc     crates/chat-stasher/src/main.rs:1156  Chrome/Chromium/Edge/Brave/Vivaldi extension id.
help_doc     crates/chat-stasher/src/main.rs:1159  Firefox add-on id (`browser_specific_settings.gecko.id`).
help_doc     crates/chat-stasher/src/main.rs:1162  Remove the manifests this command writes — and nothing else.
help_doc     crates/chat-stasher/src/main.rs:1165  Windows only: skip the `reg.exe` step and only write the JSON.
help_doc     crates/chat-stasher/src/main.rs:1168  Stage the browser-spawned host is allowed to write to. Recorded in
help_doc     crates/chat-stasher/src/main.rs:1169  the config as `[native_host] stage`. The directory must already
help_doc     crates/chat-stasher/src/main.rs:1170  exist and be a directory: the host never creates a stage, and a
help_doc     crates/chat-stasher/src/main.rs:1171  stage that appears because a host was pointed at it is a stage
help_doc     crates/chat-stasher/src/main.rs:1172  nothing pushes. The edit preserves the config file's comments and
help_doc     crates/chat-stasher/src/main.rs:1173  everything else in it.
help_doc     crates/chat-stasher/src/main.rs:1177  The Native Messaging host process itself.
help_doc     crates/chat-stasher/src/main.rs:1178
help_doc     crates/chat-stasher/src/main.rs:1179  Runs the same one-request-one-response loop the browser launch uses:
help_doc     crates/chat-stasher/src/main.rs:1180  reads one length-prefixed request frame from stdin, writes one response
help_doc     crates/chat-stasher/src/main.rs:1181  frame to stdout, exits 0. Useful for driving the host by hand before any
help_doc     crates/chat-stasher/src/main.rs:1182  browser is involved. Each process serves exactly one request — the
help_doc     crates/chat-stasher/src/main.rs:1183  browser starts one process per message, and the host is built for that.
help_doc     crates/chat-stasher/src/main.rs:1184
help_doc     crates/chat-stasher/src/main.rs:1185  Nothing but that one frame may ever reach stdout: Chromium reads stdout
help_doc     crates/chat-stasher/src/main.rs:1186  as a `u32` frame length, so a stray log line is read as a multi-gigabyte
help_doc     crates/chat-stasher/src/main.rs:1187  frame and kills the pipe. Diagnostics go to stderr. A frame that ends
help_doc     crates/chat-stasher/src/main.rs:1188  early (EOF inside the length prefix or the body) is answered with
help_doc     crates/chat-stasher/src/main.rs:1189  silence and a non-zero exit, never with a response.
help_doc     crates/chat-stasher/src/main.rs:1190
help_doc     crates/chat-stasher/src/main.rs:1191  `--self-test` prints one line of JSON on stdout and exits 0, unchanged:
help_doc     crates/chat-stasher/src/main.rs:1192  it answers "does the host process start at all?" without needing a
help_doc     crates/chat-stasher/src/main.rs:1193  request.
help_doc     crates/chat-stasher/src/main.rs:1195  Print one line of JSON describing this host, then exit 0.
help_doc     crates/chat-stasher/src/main.rs:1199  Build the activity sidecar index for one machine partition (ADR-017).
help_doc     crates/chat-stasher/src/main.rs:1200
help_doc     crates/chat-stasher/src/main.rs:1201  Walks `<stage>/sessions/<machine>/<session>/<bucket>/NNNNNN.jsonl`,
help_doc     crates/chat-stasher/src/main.rs:1202  concatenates each session's shards in global sequence order, and feeds
help_doc     crates/chat-stasher/src/main.rs:1203  every line through the conversation-time extractor to produce one
help_doc     crates/chat-stasher/src/main.rs:1204  `ActivityRow` per session. The rows are written as JSONL to
help_doc     crates/chat-stasher/src/main.rs:1205  `<stage>/meta/<machine>/activity-v1.jsonl` — the file the `overview`
help_doc     crates/chat-stasher/src/main.rs:1206  command reads back out of a destination.
help_doc     crates/chat-stasher/src/main.rs:1207
help_doc     crates/chat-stasher/src/main.rs:1208  With `--rebuild --destination`, the index is rebuilt from the archive,
help_doc     crates/chat-stasher/src/main.rs:1209  which is all a machine whose stage is gone still needs: no source
help_doc     crates/chat-stasher/src/main.rs:1210  machine, and no copy of its stage.
help_doc     crates/chat-stasher/src/main.rs:1211
help_doc     crates/chat-stasher/src/main.rs:1212  What that rebuild does depends on which partition is named and on
help_doc     crates/chat-stasher/src/main.rs:1213  whether there is a stage to restore into, because a partition's index is
help_doc     crates/chat-stasher/src/main.rs:1214  written by the machine that owns it (ADR-017):
help_doc     crates/chat-stasher/src/main.rs:1215
help_doc     crates/chat-stasher/src/main.rs:1216  * **This machine's own partition, with a `--stage` directory** — every
help_doc     crates/chat-stasher/src/main.rs:1217    archived session is restored to a temporary child of it, the full
help_doc     crates/chat-stasher/src/main.rs:1218    index is rebuilt and a new complete snapshot is appended. Existing
help_doc     crates/chat-stasher/src/main.rs:1219    snapshots stay immutable; nothing is pushed until the scan and every
help_doc     crates/chat-stasher/src/main.rs:1220    restore finish. A same-machine snapshot found before publication
help_doc     crates/chat-stasher/src/main.rs:1221    restarts the rebuild so the appended snapshot cannot hide it.
help_doc     crates/chat-stasher/src/main.rs:1222  * **Any other machine, or any machine when there is no stage directory
help_doc     crates/chat-stasher/src/main.rs:1223    to restore into** — the rebuild is **read-only**. That machine's
help_doc     crates/chat-stasher/src/main.rs:1224    archived sessions are read cumulatively across its snapshots and the
help_doc     crates/chat-stasher/src/main.rs:1225    rows are written to a derived index in this machine's cache (the path
help_doc     crates/chat-stasher/src/main.rs:1226    is printed). The destination is not modified at all: no snapshot is
help_doc     crates/chat-stasher/src/main.rs:1227    appended and no path in the named machine's partition is written,
help_doc     crates/chat-stasher/src/main.rs:1228    because no record authorizes one machine to rewrite another's.
help_doc     crates/chat-stasher/src/main.rs:1229
help_doc     crates/chat-stasher/src/main.rs:1230  Both modes are safe to re-run, and neither is resumable: each run starts
help_doc     crates/chat-stasher/src/main.rs:1231  over. A read-only run needs the destination and the masterkey, and no
help_doc     crates/chat-stasher/src/main.rs:1232  `--stage` at all — which is how a machine whose stage is gone, this one
help_doc     crates/chat-stasher/src/main.rs:1233  included, still derives its index from the archive.
help_doc     crates/chat-stasher/src/main.rs:1234
help_doc     crates/chat-stasher/src/main.rs:1235  The harness label is inferred from the session directory name: the
help_doc     crates/chat-stasher/src/main.rs:1236  canonical archived ids are `<source>.<machine>.<native-id>`, so the
help_doc     crates/chat-stasher/src/main.rs:1237  harness is the leading dot-segment (`claude-code.<m>.<uuid>` ->
help_doc     crates/chat-stasher/src/main.rs:1238  `claude-code`); short forms are handled too (`opencode~abc123` ->
help_doc     crates/chat-stasher/src/main.rs:1239  `opencode`, `cursor.d~xxx` -> `cursor`).
help_doc     crates/chat-stasher/src/main.rs:1240
help_doc     crates/chat-stasher/src/main.rs:1241  Metadata, with one declared exception: the extraction keeps a timestamp
help_doc     crates/chat-stasher/src/main.rs:1242  per line and throws the line away, and — for claude-code sessions —
help_doc     crates/chat-stasher/src/main.rs:1243  additionally keeps the capped one-line label the dashboard lists the
help_doc     crates/chat-stasher/src/main.rs:1244  session under (the harness's own title, or the head of the session's
help_doc     crates/chat-stasher/src/main.rs:1245  first user line; see the `ui` labels). That label — at most 100
help_doc     crates/chat-stasher/src/main.rs:1246  characters, with its provenance — is the one piece of
help_doc     crates/chat-stasher/src/main.rs:1247  conversation-derived text the metadata tier ever holds. Nothing else is
help_doc     crates/chat-stasher/src/main.rs:1248  ever kept, and the report is counts and the output path only.
help_doc     crates/chat-stasher/src/main.rs:1249
help_doc     crates/chat-stasher/src/main.rs:1250  Exit codes: `0` = the whole partition was read and the index written;
help_doc     crates/chat-stasher/src/main.rs:1251  `3` = the stage could not be read (or reading was interrupted) — nothing
help_doc     crates/chat-stasher/src/main.rs:1252  (complete) was written; `1` = every session was read but the index file
help_doc     crates/chat-stasher/src/main.rs:1253  itself could not be written; `2` = usage error. Same family as
help_doc     crates/chat-stasher/src/main.rs:1254  `collect`/`search`: `3` means "did not finish / never started", `1`
help_doc     crates/chat-stasher/src/main.rs:1255  means "finished and then failed".
help_doc     crates/chat-stasher/src/main.rs:1257  Local stage directory, or an existing workspace directory for a
help_doc     crates/chat-stasher/src/main.rs:1258  destination rebuild of **this** machine's own partition (temporary
help_doc     crates/chat-stasher/src/main.rs:1259  restored shards are removed after the new snapshot is written).
help_doc     crates/chat-stasher/src/main.rs:1260  Omitted, or not a directory, the rebuild restores nothing and is
help_doc     crates/chat-stasher/src/main.rs:1261  read-only for any machine, this one included.
help_doc     crates/chat-stasher/src/main.rs:1264  Machine partition for `sessions/<machine>/…`.
help_doc     crates/chat-stasher/src/main.rs:1265  Default: config `machine`, else this machine's identity (generated
help_doc     crates/chat-stasher/src/main.rs:1266  on first use); use `--machine` explicitly to choose the partition.
help_doc     crates/chat-stasher/src/main.rs:1269  Explicitly rebuild the complete partition index. The command has
help_doc     crates/chat-stasher/src/main.rs:1270  always rebuilt rather than incrementally patched; this spelling is
help_doc     crates/chat-stasher/src/main.rs:1271  provided for repair workflows and makes that intent visible.
help_doc     crates/chat-stasher/src/main.rs:1274  Destination to rebuild from. Requires `--rebuild`; either this or
help_doc     crates/chat-stasher/src/main.rs:1275  `--repo` must be named. Appends the repaired snapshot when the named
help_doc     crates/chat-stasher/src/main.rs:1276  `--machine` is this machine's own partition and `--stage` is a
help_doc     crates/chat-stasher/src/main.rs:1277  directory; otherwise the rebuild is read-only and the result goes to
help_doc     crates/chat-stasher/src/main.rs:1278  a derived local index.
help_doc     crates/chat-stasher/src/main.rs:1281  Repository path override for destination rebuilds.
help_doc     crates/chat-stasher/src/main.rs:1284  Masterkey file override for destination rebuilds.
help_doc     crates/chat-stasher/src/main.rs:1287  Concurrency cap override for destination rebuilds.
help_doc     crates/chat-stasher/src/main.rs:1290  Backend option `key=value`, repeatable.
help_doc     crates/chat-stasher/src/main.rs:1293  Keep ssh ControlMaster processes open after this run.
help_doc     crates/chat-stasher/src/main.rs:1297  Write this machine's display-name declaration (ADR-018).
help_doc     crates/chat-stasher/src/main.rs:1298
help_doc     crates/chat-stasher/src/main.rs:1299  Writes `<stage>/meta/<machine>/machine.json` — a `MachineDeclaration`
help_doc     crates/chat-stasher/src/main.rs:1300  that carries the human display name, the OS and a first-seen time. The
help_doc     crates/chat-stasher/src/main.rs:1301  machine partition is resolved exactly like every other command: config
help_doc     crates/chat-stasher/src/main.rs:1302  `machine` first, then the identity file (generated when missing). The
help_doc     crates/chat-stasher/src/main.rs:1303  next `push` archives the whole stage root, so this file rides along.
help_doc     crates/chat-stasher/src/main.rs:1304
help_doc     crates/chat-stasher/src/main.rs:1305  The display name is taken from `--display-name` when given; otherwise
help_doc     crates/chat-stasher/src/main.rs:1306  the system's LocalHostName (`scutil --get LocalHostName` on macOS,
help_doc     crates/chat-stasher/src/main.rs:1307  `hostname` elsewhere) is used. If neither is available the field is
help_doc     crates/chat-stasher/src/main.rs:1308  written **empty** and the command says so — a name is never invented.
help_doc     crates/chat-stasher/src/main.rs:1309
help_doc     crates/chat-stasher/src/main.rs:1310  Exit codes: `0` = the declaration was written; `3` = the machine
help_doc     crates/chat-stasher/src/main.rs:1311  partition could not be resolved or the identity is unusable; `1` = the
help_doc     crates/chat-stasher/src/main.rs:1312  file could not be written; `2` = usage error.
help_doc     crates/chat-stasher/src/main.rs:1314  Stage directory to write the declaration into (`<stage>/meta/…`).
help_doc     crates/chat-stasher/src/main.rs:1317  Human display name for this machine. Default: system LocalHostName.
help_doc     crates/chat-stasher/src/main.rs:1321  Give a dead or sold machine a display name (ADR-018).
help_doc     crates/chat-stasher/src/main.rs:1322
help_doc     crates/chat-stasher/src/main.rs:1323  Writes `<stage>/meta/<target>/label-by-<local-identity>.json` — a
help_doc     crates/chat-stasher/src/main.rs:1324  `LabelRecord` expressing *this* machine's opinion about what `<target>`
help_doc     crates/chat-stasher/src/main.rs:1325  should be called. It exists for machines that can no longer declare for
help_doc     crates/chat-stasher/src/main.rs:1326  themselves (sold, dead, in a different building). Each file has exactly
help_doc     crates/chat-stasher/src/main.rs:1327  one writer, so concurrent machines never fight over it; the overview

help_doc     crates/chat-stasher/src/main.rs:1329

help_doc     crates/chat-stasher/src/main.rs:1331  not be resolved; `1` = the file could not be written; `2` = usage error.

help_doc     crates/chat-stasher/src/main.rs:1343  Draw the machine × harness activity overview of one destination
help_doc     crates/chat-stasher/src/main.rs:1344  (ADR-017).
help_doc     crates/chat-stasher/src/main.rs:1345
help_doc     crates/chat-stasher/src/main.rs:1346  Opens the destination repository, takes each host's newest snapshot
help_doc     crates/chat-stasher/src/main.rs:1347  (the same cross-machine merge as `read --all-machines`), and for every
help_doc     crates/chat-stasher/src/main.rs:1348  snapshot recursively finds the activity index files at

help_doc     crates/chat-stasher/src/main.rs:1351  `meta` / `<machine>` / `activity-v1.jsonl` marker — never by a local
help_doc     crates/chat-stasher/src/main.rs:1352  path. The indexes are parsed into overview rows and rendered as a
help_doc     crates/chat-stasher/src/main.rs:1353  machine × harness matrix, a time-unknown tally and a width-adaptive
help_doc     crates/chat-stasher/src/main.rs:1354  heatmap. Prints counts, machine names and time spans only — never
help_doc     crates/chat-stasher/src/main.rs:1355  conversation content.
help_doc     crates/chat-stasher/src/main.rs:1356
help_doc     crates/chat-stasher/src/main.rs:1357  A machine that has a snapshot but **no** activity index is listed
help_doc     crates/chat-stasher/src/main.rs:1358  explicitly as "index missing" — it never vanishes silently, because a missing
help_doc     crates/chat-stasher/src/main.rs:1359  index is not the same thing as "that machine had no sessions".
help_doc     crates/chat-stasher/src/main.rs:1360
help_doc     crates/chat-stasher/src/main.rs:1361  Exit codes: `0` = at least one index was read and rendered; `1` = the
help_doc     crates/chat-stasher/src/main.rs:1362  whole repository was read and there is no activity index at all (a real
help_doc     crates/chat-stasher/src/main.rs:1363  "there is none", not a failure to look); `3` = the repository could not
help_doc     crates/chat-stasher/src/main.rs:1364  be read in full (open / snapshot / tree / dump failure) — the absences
help_doc     crates/chat-stasher/src/main.rs:1365  below are unproven; `2` = usage error.

help_doc     crates/chat-stasher/src/main.rs:1368  there is no default destination.
help_doc     crates/chat-stasher/src/main.rs:1371  Terminal width for the matrix/heatmap (default: 100).

help_doc     crates/chat-stasher/src/main.rs:1379  (read in full, no index anywhere); a failed read (exit 3) puts the

help_doc     crates/chat-stasher/src/main.rs:1383  With `--json`, emit the aggregate summary variant instead of the

help_doc     crates/chat-stasher/src/main.rs:1405  Manage this machine's body cache (ADR-034).
help_doc     crates/chat-stasher/src/main.rs:1406
help_doc     crates/chat-stasher/src/main.rs:1407  The body cache holds the conversation bodies a read would otherwise pull
help_doc     crates/chat-stasher/src/main.rs:1408  from a destination again, as the destination's own ciphertext. It is
help_doc     crates/chat-stasher/src/main.rs:1409  disposable by design: nothing here is part of the archive, and deleting
help_doc     crates/chat-stasher/src/main.rs:1410  all of it changes nothing except how long the next read takes. Without a
help_doc     crates/chat-stasher/src/main.rs:1411  subcommand it prints the location, the quota and the current occupancy,
help_doc     crates/chat-stasher/src/main.rs:1412  so a cache you never meant to have is visible before you clear it.
help_doc     crates/chat-stasher/src/main.rs:1414  What to do; omit to see the current occupancy.
help_doc     crates/chat-stasher/src/main.rs:1418  Build or inspect the per-destination local full-text index.
help_doc     crates/chat-stasher/src/main.rs:1425  `cache` subcommands.

help_doc     crates/chat-stasher/src/main.rs:1429
help_doc     crates/chat-stasher/src/main.rs:1430  Only the cache directory is touched — never the archive, never a
help_doc     crates/chat-stasher/src/main.rs:1431  destination, never a key. Entries are re-fetched from the destination
help_doc     crates/chat-stasher/src/main.rs:1432  the next time a session is read.

help_doc     crates/chat-stasher/src/main.rs:1570  The parameters of the remote step, exactly as the caller supplied them.
help_doc     crates/chat-stasher/src/main.rs:1571
help_doc     crates/chat-stasher/src/main.rs:1572  Every field here is either a name or a location. **No field can carry a
help_doc     crates/chat-stasher/src/main.rs:1573  secret**, and that is the point of the shape rather than an accident of it:
help_doc     crates/chat-stasher/src/main.rs:1574  the two credential fields are the *names of environment variables*, which the
help_doc     crates/chat-stasher/src/main.rs:1575  wizard writes into the config as `env:NAME` and never resolves itself. So a
help_doc     crates/chat-stasher/src/main.rs:1576  secret cannot reach the config file as plaintext, and it cannot reach
help_doc     crates/chat-stasher/src/main.rs:1577  `argv` — where it would be captured by the process list and by any log that
help_doc     crates/chat-stasher/src/main.rs:1578  echoes the command — because there is no flag that would accept one.
help_doc     crates/chat-stasher/src/main.rs:1581  Which recipe to write.
help_doc     crates/chat-stasher/src/main.rs:1584  SFTP: `ssh://<host>:<port>`. S3: the service endpoint, e.g.
help_doc     crates/chat-stasher/src/main.rs:1585  `https://<account-id>.r2.cloudflarestorage.com`.
help_doc     crates/chat-stasher/src/main.rs:1588  SFTP only: the ssh user.
help_doc     crates/chat-stasher/src/main.rs:1591  SFTP only: the private key to authenticate with. Optional — leaving it
help_doc     crates/chat-stasher/src/main.rs:1592  out lets the backend use the ssh agent and its own default keys, which is
help_doc     crates/chat-stasher/src/main.rs:1593  a real configuration rather than a gap.
help_doc     crates/chat-stasher/src/main.rs:1596  S3 only: the bucket (or container) the repository lives in.
help_doc     crates/chat-stasher/src/main.rs:1599  S3 only: the region. R2 is single-region and names it `auto`; another
help_doc     crates/chat-stasher/src/main.rs:1600  S3-compatible service names its own.
help_doc     crates/chat-stasher/src/main.rs:1603  Both kinds: the prefix inside the account/bucket that the repository
help_doc     crates/chat-stasher/src/main.rs:1604  lives under. Optional, and omitted rather than defaulted: a prefix the
help_doc     crates/chat-stasher/src/main.rs:1605  user did not choose would put their archive somewhere they did not name.
help_doc     crates/chat-stasher/src/main.rs:1608  S3 only: **the name of** the environment variable holding the access key
help_doc     crates/chat-stasher/src/main.rs:1609  id. Not the key id itself.
help_doc     crates/chat-stasher/src/main.rs:1612  S3 only: **the name of** the environment variable holding the secret
help_doc     crates/chat-stasher/src/main.rs:1613  access key. Not the secret.
help_doc     crates/chat-stasher/src/main.rs:1616  Declare that this host's key was checked out of band, which authorizes
help_doc     crates/chat-stasher/src/main.rs:1617  recording it in `~/.ssh/known_hosts`. A declaration, not a verification:
help_doc     crates/chat-stasher/src/main.rs:1618  nothing here, and nothing anywhere else, can check that the comparison
